When the credential was registered. Required by the task, and the same
instant recorded on the stored `RegisteredPasskey`, so a client need
not re-list to learn it.

subject.description:
The DID this passkey now authenticates.

Required by `auth/passkey/enroll/finish/0.2` and absent until #1112.
A caller enrolling on behalf of someone else had no way to confirm
*whose* credential it just created — the response named the credential
and not the subject, which is the half that matters for an audit trail.

RegisterResponse.description:
`{ endorsementType: … }` — the shape `vtc/endorsement-types/register/0.1`
publishes. The handler returned the bare row until #1059's witness
compared it with its own schema; the row itself conformed.

enrollmentId.description:
Opaque id the operator passes back to `enroll/finish`.

`enrollmentId`, the name the task publishes — it was `registrationId`
until #1112.

options.description:
The value for `navigator.credentials.create({ publicKey: … })`.

The **inner** options, not webauthn-rs's `{publicKey: …}` wrapper.
`CredentialCreationOptions` in the published schema describes itself as
"server-issued options for `navigator.credentials.create({ publicKey:
... })`" — the value that goes *inside* the key, not the object
containing it.

uvOptions.description:
The value for `navigator.credentials.get({ publicKey: … })` for the
step-up assertion against an existing passkey. Unwrapped for the same
reason as `options`.

RegisteredCredential.description:
The wire view of a passkey, as `auth/passkey/list/0.1` publishes it.

Separate from [`RegisteredPasskey`] because that type is a **storage row**:
it is `Deserialize`d out of the `admin:<did>` record, so its member names
are the on-disk format and renaming them would orphan every passkey already
enrolled. The two shapes disagree in exactly the two ways the schema cares
about, and both differences are the storage row's to keep:

- `label` is published as `deviceLabel`, and is **absent** rather than empty
  when nobody chose one. The schema is explicit that a consumer must not
  synthesize a label, "because an invented one is indistinguishable from a
  chosen one to somebody deciding which credential to revoke" — and `""` is
  an invented one.
- `lastUsedAt` is omitted when unset. Sending `null` is a type error against
  a `date-time` member, and the schema notes it deliberately does not
  distinguish "never used" from "not tracked", since no binding could carry
  the difference anyway.

RegistryStatus.description:
Wire-form status for [`RegistryRecord::status`]. Mirrors the
`status ∈ { Active, Departed }` enumeration in spec §5.7.

RegistryTransport.description:
How the VTC reaches its trust registry, as an operator sees it.

The two protocol fields answer different questions, and reporting only one
of them is what made the old `registry_status` misleading:

- `advertised` — what the registry's **DID document** says it speaks. Read
  from the document, which is the authority (CLAUDE.md), so an operator can
  see the registry's own claim without resolving the DID by hand.
- `active` — what the last selection actually **chose**, which is the
  highest-preference protocol present in both parties' documents. Empty
  until the first call; `error` says why if selection failed.

Advertised without active means the two sides have no transport in common,
or nothing has tried yet — a distinction a single "protocol" field cannot
express, and precisely the state that leaves a registry looking configured
while nothing can reach it.

active.description:
The protocol the last selection chose. `None` before the first call, or
when selection failed — see `error`.

advertised.description:
Protocols the registry's DID document advertises, in preference order
(`tsp`, `didcomm`, `rest`). Empty when the DID has not been resolved
yet, or when the registry is addressed by URL alone.

did.description: The registry's DID, when it is addressed by one.

error.description: Why the last selection failed, if it did.

url.description: The registry's REST base URL, when one is configured.

ReloadResponse.description:
`POST /v1/admin/config/reload` response. Lists the keys whose
**db-layer** values were applied in-memory by this call. Keys
flagged `requires_restart` never appear here — they re-apply on
the next restart.

RemovedMember.description:
A departed member whose Member row was retained (Tombstone / Historical
disposition) after its ACL was deleted. Surfaced so operators can see who
left and purge the lingering rows.

status.description: Always `"removed"` — present so the UI can render a uniform status.

statusListIndex.description: Revocation slot the member held (for audit / re-flip), if any.

RemovedMembersResponse.description:
`{ removed: [...] }` — the shape `vtc/members/removed/0.1` publishes.

The handler returned a top-level array until #1059's witness compared it
with its schema. The rows themselves always conformed.

reason.description: Optional operator note ("renewal", "audit", …) relayed to the member.

requested.description:
Always `true` — the request was dispatched to the member's agent. The
member replies asynchronously over `members/vmc/1.0`.

threadId.description: DIDComm thread id of the dispatched request, for correlation.

RestartResponse.description:
`POST /v1/admin/config/restart` response when the supervisor
check passes.

drainTimeoutSeconds.description:
`drain_timeout` (seconds) the daemon will use for graceful
shutdown. Mirrors `RestartRequestedData.drain_timeout_seconds`.

supervisor.description:
Which supervisor the daemon detected (so the operator's
admin UX can echo it back).

RevocationDetail.description: The credential the revocation applies to, and when it took effect.

RevocationReviewState.description: Whether a withdrawn statement touches a standing membership.

remaining.description:
How many passkeys the subject has left.

Required by `auth/passkey/revoke/finish/0.1` and absent until #1112.
It is the number the caller most needs and the one this endpoint is
uniquely placed to give: the last-passkey guard refuses to leave an
admin at zero, so a client that cannot see the count cannot tell
whether the next revoke will succeed without attempting it.

RevokeSessionResponse.description: `auth/revoke-session/0.2#response` — how many sessions the call ended.

uvOptions.description:
Unwrapped, as everywhere else in this family — the value for
`navigator.credentials.get({ publicKey: … })`.

Session.description:
Canonical `Session` from `spec/auth/_shared/0.1/session.schema.json`.

Aligns with OIDC Core §2 / RFC 8176:
- `amr`: authentication method references. VTI vocabulary uses
  `"did"` (challenge-response), `"passkey"` (WebAuthn assertion),
  `"vta"` (verifiable-trust-agent approval).
- `acr`: authentication context class reference. Typical values
  `"aal1"` (single-factor DID), `"aal2"` (second possession/
  biometric factor), `"aal3"` (hardware-bound second factor).

expiresAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the session ceases to be valid.

issuedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the session was created.

SessionListResponse.description: `auth/sessions/list/0.1#response` — the sessions the caller may see.

sessions.description: Newest first (`issuedAt` descending), as the specification recommends.

acr.description: Authentication context class per OIDC Core §2, when recorded.

amr.description: Authentication methods per RFC 8176, when the token records any.

issuedAt.description:
When the session was issued — the JWT's `iat`, required by the
component and simply never surfaced before.

Severity.description: How loudly a [`Finding`] should be reported.

ShowWhen.description:
A `showWhen` predicate, declarative so it crosses the wire: render
the field only when `field`'s value equals `eq` (or its truthiness
matches `truthy`).

SubmittedAttribute.description:
One answer an applicant gave to the manifest's `requestedAttributes`: a
claim type and its value, as they sent it.

TokenBundle.description:
Canonical `TokenBundle` from `spec/auth/_shared/0.1/tokens.schema.json`.

OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749 §5.1)-shaped: `expiresIn` is seconds from
issuance, not an absolute timestamp. Clients compute the absolute
expiry as `now() + expires_in` immediately after issuance, or
store the issuance moment alongside the bundle.

TransportStatus.description:
One transport's public connectivity status, as reported on the
unauthenticated community profile.

The two flags answer different questions and both are needed:

- `advertised` — will a client resolving this community's DID *find* this
  transport? Read from the DID document, which is the authority (CLAUDE.md).
- `serviceable` — if reached on it, can this VTC actually answer? Build
  capability plus live messaging connectivity.

A transport is genuinely reachable only when **both** are true. Splitting
them is the point: the failure that motivated all of this was `advertised`

VtcDirectoryCardPublicV0_1DigestMultibas.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.

VtcDirectoryCardPublicV0_1EntryId.description: Opaque identifier of one directory entry: `dir_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random, scoped to one community, and stable for the life of the membership — it survives a rotation of the member's DID, which is why groups, notes and cards are keyed by it. It MUST NOT be derived from, and MUST NOT reveal, any DID of the member, and the same person's entries in two communities MUST NOT share one. Compared by exact string equality.

VtcDirectoryCardPublicV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcDirectoryCardPublicV0_1Payload.description: Read a member's external card, as they signed it. Anyone may ask; the request carries nothing about the reader. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

VtcDirectoryCardPublicV0_1PublishedCard.description:
A member's external card: a JSContact `Card` (RFC 9553) holding exactly their values whose visibility is `public`, mapped as `JSContactCard` maps them, with the member's W3C Data Integrity `proof`. The community serves it as received and never signs, composes or edits it (VTI-REG-004 item 4).

Carried as an open object, and deliberately so: the proof covers every member of the card, and a typed binding that kept only the members named here would drop the rest and break the signature. So this schema constrains none of its members, and a consumer MUST check them itself: `@type`, `version`, `uid`, `issuer` and `proof` are present; `@type` is `Card`; `version` is `1.0`; `uid` is `urn:vtc-directory:<EntryId>`; `issuer` is the member's membership DID; `proof` is a `DataIntegrityProof` with `cryptosuite` `eddsa-jcs-2022` or `ecdsa-jcs-2019`, `proofPurpose` `assertionMethod`, and a `verificationMethod` of the member's membership DID authorized for `assertionMethod`; and the proof verifies over the card without it, before any member is relied on.

external.description: Whether the member publishes a public card — the fields whose visibility is `public`, signed by the member — through the community's trust registry. A second consent, separate from registry-publication consent (`publishConsent`), which it requires. A community that cannot yet publish external cards refuses `true` with `notAvailable`.

search.description: What a member's search may match. `byName`: `displayName` or `nickname`. `exactNickname`: only an exact `nickname`. `off`: nothing. A DID is never a search key for a non-administrator, whatever this says.

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1EntryId.description: Opaque identifier of one directory entry: `dir_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random, scoped to one community, and stable for the life of the membership — it survives a rotation of the member's DID, which is why groups, notes and cards are keyed by it. It MUST NOT be derived from, and MUST NOT reveal, any DID of the member, and the same person's entries in two communities MUST NOT share one. Compared by exact string equality.

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1ExternalCard.description: Where the member's external card stands. Present on a card exactly when `discoverability.external` is true. `published`: the community is serving the card the member signed, and its trust registry points to it. `awaitingSignature`: the member's `public` values have changed since they signed, so the community has withdrawn the card it was serving and serves none until the member signs the current values (vtc/directory/card/publish). The community never serves a card the member did not sign, and never one that differs from their current `public` values.

publishedAt.description: Present while `published`: when the card now served was published.

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1FieldKey.description: Identifier of a directory field. A key with no `.` is a BASE field, the same in every community: `displayName`, `nickname`, `avatar`, `pronouns`, `bio`, `links` (written by the member) and `role`, `joinedAt`, `did`, `personhood` (derived from the community's own records, never stored on a card). A community-defined field MUST use a reverse-DNS key (`org.example.employer`), so a base key never collides with one, and a key is never reused with a different meaning once defined.

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1FieldValue.description: The value of one field. Which shape a field takes is fixed by its definition's `type`: text-like types (`text`, `longText`, `url`, `email`, `phone`, `enum`, `date` as YYYY-MM-DD, `country` as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, `did`) are strings; `multiEnum` and the base field `links` are arrays of strings; `image` and the base field `avatar` are a `CardBlobRef`; `claim` is a `VerifiedValue`; the derived base field `personhood` is a boolean.

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1FieldVisibilit.description: The audience the member chose for each field. A field with no entry here takes its definition's `defaultVisibility`. The community MUST NOT widen a member's choice: widening a field's ceiling or default changes no visibility already recorded.

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1GroupId.description: Opaque identifier of a community group: `grp_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random and community-scoped; not the group's DID.

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1Introductions.description: Who may ask the community to introduce them to this member. `anyone`: any active member who can find the entry. `groups`: only members who share a community group with them. `connections`: only members holding an attributed, in-force verified relationship with them. `off`: nobody. A refused introduction is never reported to its sender.

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1Listing.description: Whether members can find the entry. `listed`: it appears when members browse. `findable`: it does not appear when browsing, but a search that matches it under `search` returns it. `hidden`: no member finds it by browsing or searching; administrators still see it, and members who share a group that shows its members see it in that group's member list.

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1Payload.description: A member changes their own directory card: values they write themselves, the visibility of each field, their discoverability and who may ask to be introduced to them. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

expectedRevision.description: Optional: apply only if the card is at this revision, else refuse with `superseded`.

groupAudience.description: Replaces the groups that count as the `groups` audience; `null` returns to every group the member is in.

values.description: Values to set, keyed by field; `null` clears one. Fields not named are unchanged. Only `member`-sourced fields.

visibility.description: Visibilities to set, keyed by field; `null` returns a field to its default. Applies to any non-derived field on the card, whoever wrote its value, and to the derived fields the community lets a member widen (`did`).

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/directory/card/update/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/directory/card/update/0.1#response.

VtcDirectoryCardUpdateV0_1VerifiedValue.description: The value of a `credential`-sourced field: a claim the member disclosed from a credential they presented, with the issuer that attests it. A verified value always names its issuer, and a self-asserted value is never shaped as one. The community keeps only the disclosed claim and these facts about it — never the presentation.

credentialType.description: The most specific `type` of the credential the claim came from.

issuer.description: DID of the credential's issuer, shown as the field's verification badge.

validUntil.description: When the credential expires, where it does. The community withdraws the value once it passes.

verifiedAt.description: When the community verified the presentation.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1Audience.description:
Who may see a directory field, ordered from narrowest to widest. `admins`: holders of `vtc.directory.admin` (and, for derived fields, `vtc.members.manage`). `groups`: members who share at least one community group with the subject (narrowed to the groups the subject names in `groupAudience`, where it names any). `connections`: members holding an attributed, in-force verified relationship with the subject at the community. `members`: every active member. `public`: anyone, and what the member's signed public card carries outside the community.

`groups` and `connections` are not a chain: a viewer sees a field when they satisfy the audience the subject chose for it or any wider audience. Every audience includes the administrators, and the subject always sees their own whole card. There is no `onlyMe`: a value nobody else should see is not directory data.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1DigestMultibas.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1DirectoryDiscl.description: The statement itself. Every member is generated from the community's configuration when the statement is read. `statementDigest` names this exact statement, so an applicant can record which one it was shown.

adminNotes.description: Whether administrators keep notes about members. Notes are never on a card and never reach another member; a member may ask for the notes about them.

externalCards.description: Whether a member may publish a card beyond the community: their `public` values, signed by them, offered through the community's trust registry. Always the member's own choice, and off on a new card. False where the community cannot publish external cards.

fields.description: Every active field, base and community-defined, in display order. A base field the community has disabled is absent, which is how a reader learns it is not collected.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1DisclosedField.description: One active field of the community's directory, as an applicant needs to see it: what it is, who writes its value, the widest audience it may ever reach and the audience a new card gives it. Disabled and retired fields are not listed: no projection shows them.

facet.description: Whether members may filter on the field and see counts by its values. Absent: false.

searchable.description: Whether a member's search may match the field, within what the searcher may see.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1FieldDescripti.description: Help text shown to a member filling the field in. Plain text; a reader MUST NOT treat it as instructions.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1FieldKey.description: Identifier of a directory field. A key with no `.` is a BASE field, the same in every community: `displayName`, `nickname`, `avatar`, `pronouns`, `bio`, `links` (written by the member) and `role`, `joinedAt`, `did`, `personhood` (derived from the community's own records, never stored on a card). VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1FieldLabel.description: What readers see as the field's name. Plain text.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1FieldSource.description: Who writes the value. `member`: self-asserted, through vtc/directory/card/update. `admin`: asserted by the community through vtc/directory/card/assert; the member reads it and cannot change it. `credential`: a claim the member discloses from a credential through vtc/directory/card/present, badged with its issuer. `derived`: a base field read from the community's own records (`role`, `joinedAt`, `did`, `personhood`) and never stored on a card. VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1FieldType.description: The kind of value a field holds, which fixes its `FieldValue` shape. `did` holds a DID the member chooses to show (never their membership DID, which is the derived base field `did`). `claim` holds a `VerifiedValue` and requires `source: credential`.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1GroupDisclosur.description: Present when the community has groups. A member of a group holds a credential, issued by the group's own identifier, that evidences their membership, and can present it outside the community — which is why an applicant is told.

credentialValidity.description: How long each group membership credential is valid for, as an ISO 8601 duration in weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds (`P30D`). It is renewed while the member stays in the group, and a credential already issued stays valid until it expires even after its holder leaves.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1NewCardDefault.description: The discoverability a card has when the community creates it, before its member chooses. A new card is never published beyond the community (VTI-DIR-042), so there is no member for that here: `externalCards` says whether the member may turn it on.

search.description: What a member's search may match, as the card's `discoverability.search`.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1Payload.description: Read the statement of what a community's directory discloses about its members, and to whom, generated from the configuration in force. Anyone may read it, applicants above all, so the request carries nothing about the reader. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

VtcDirectoryDisclosureV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/directory/disclosure/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/directory/disclosure/0.1#response.

VtcDirectoryEntriesListV0_1CardBlobRef.description: A content-addressed image held in the community's blob store — an avatar or an `image` field. At most 256 KiB, images only, re-encoded by the community on upload (vtc/directory/images/upload: metadata stripped, dimensions capped) so its digest does not link the member across communities. A viewer reads the bytes with vtc/directory/images/get, which answers only where the same projection shows the value. `url` and `urlExpiresAt` MAY appear in a projection: a short-lived URL the community checks against the same projection, so a member-only image is never a public URL. A community that does not offer one leaves both out.

mediaType.description: Media type of the stored bytes.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the stored, re-encoded bytes.

size.description: Size in bytes of the stored bytes.

url.description: Projection only: a URL the viewer can fetch the image from until `urlExpiresAt`.

VtcDirectoryEntriesListV0_1DirectoryEntr.description: One entry as a particular viewer sees it.

connected.description: Present, and `true`, only when the viewer is one of the two parties to an attributed, in-force verified relationship with this entry's member that the community can see. sharedGroups.description: The community groups the viewer and this member both belong to, among those whose membership the viewer may see. Absent when there are none.

VtcDirectoryEntriesListV0_1Payload.description: Browse, search and filter a community's member directory. Each entry is projected for the caller: only fields the member, the community's ceiling and its policy all allow. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token from a previous page's `nextCursor`, valid only for the same caller and question.

filters.description: Facet filters: an entry matches when, for every filter, its value of the field is one of `values`. Only facets visible to the caller.

limit.description: Page size; the community clamps to 1..=100 (default 25).

query.description: Search text. At least three characters, or a whole nickname for an exact-nickname search.

VtcDirectoryEntriesListV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/directory/entries/list/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/directory/entries/list/0.1#response.

count.description: Matching entries. Absent when below the community's threshold.

fewerThan.description: Present instead of `count` when the count is below the threshold *k*: there are fewer than this many.

facets.description: Counts for the facets visible to the caller, over the whole result. Absent when none is.

nextCursor.description: Continuation token, or null when this is the last page.

VtcDirectoryExportV0_1JSContactCard.description: One entry exported as a JSContact `Card` (RFC 9553). Member names inside are JSContact's own and are carried verbatim. `uid` is `urn:vtc-directory:<EntryId>`. Base fields map as their definitions' `jsContactPath` says (`displayName` → `name.full`, `nickname` → `nicknames`, `avatar` → `media` of kind `photo`, `pronouns` → `speakToAs.pronouns`, `bio` → `notes`, `links` → `links`); community fields and derived fields are exported as vendor-specific properties named by their field key. Additional members are permitted because JSContact defines them. Carried as an open object so that no JSContact member is lost in transit: a consumer MUST check that `@type` is `Card`, `version` is `1.0` and `uid` is `urn:vtc-directory:<EntryId>`, which this schema does not constrain.

VtcDirectoryExportV0_1Payload.description: A directory administrator exports the whole member directory as JSContact cards, a page at a time. Members cannot export. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

format.description: The export format. Only JSContact (RFC 9553) in this version.

reason.description: Why, recorded with the change and shown to anyone who must approve it.

VtcDirectoryExportV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/directory/export/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/directory/export/0.1#response.

VtcDirectoryFieldsDefineV0_1ClaimSelecto.description: Which claim a `claim` field accepts, from which credentials and issuers.

claimPath.description: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) to the claim within `credentialSubject`.

credentialType.description: A `type` the presented credential MUST carry.

issuers.description: Issuers the community accepts for this field. Absent: the community's trusted issuers for the credential type, as its own policy decides.

label.description: What a reader is shown for it.

VtcDirectoryFieldsDefineV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcDirectoryFieldsDefineV0_1FieldConstra.description: Per-type constraints. A member that does not apply to the field's type is refused by the community with `valueInvalid` when the definition is written.

options.description: The permitted values of an `enum` or `multiEnum` field.

pattern.description: ECMA-262 regular expression a text value MUST match.

VtcDirectoryFieldsDefineV0_1FieldDefinit.description: One field of the community's directory schema, as the community holds it. The audience order `admins` < `groups`/`connections` < `members` < `public` applies to `ceiling` and `defaultVisibility`; `defaultVisibility` is never wider than `ceiling`.

base.description: `true` for a base field, present in every community; `false` for a field this community defined.

jsContactPath.description: Where the field lands when an entry is exported as a JSContact Card (RFC 9553), e.g. `name.full`, `nicknames`, `speakToAs.pronouns`. Absent: a vendor-specific property named by the key.

purgeAfter.description: When the values of a retired field are purged. Present only on a retired field.

retiredAt.description: When the field was retired. Present only on a retired field.

VtcDirectoryFieldsDefineV0_1FieldDescrip.description: Help text shown to a member filling the field in. Plain text; a reader MUST NOT treat it as instructions.

VtcDirectoryFieldsDefineV0_1FieldInput.description: What an administrator supplies to define a community field. `key`, `type` and `source` are fixed for the field's life.

facet.description: Whether the field may be filtered on and counted. Only `enum`, `multiEnum` and `country` fields may be facets. Absent: false.

required.description: Whether a card must hold a value for its entry to be listed. Never a condition of membership. Absent: false.

searchable.description: Whether a member's search may match the field, within what the searcher may see. Absent: false.

source.description: As `FieldSource`, less `derived`, which only base fields carry.

VtcGroupsBindingsAddV0_1CapabilityRef.description: A capability, optionally qualified by a resource. Used where a capability is named but not granted — a role's ceiling, a role's approve ceiling, an entry's approvable capabilities. An unqualified reference covers every resource of the capability's kind.

VtcGroupsBindingsAddV0_1GrantsBindingSpe.description: A grant set the group confers: each capability is written onto every member's access-control entry as a resource grant whose source is the group, bounded by the member's role ceiling and by the binder's own holdings.

state.description: `pending`: waiting for the consent the community requires. `active`: in force; the community's reconciler keeps members' admissions and grants in line with it. `removing`: being withdrawn; the reconciler is removing what only this binding provided.

VtcGroupsBindingsAddV0_1GroupId.description: Opaque identifier of a community group: `grp_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random and community-scoped; not the group's DID.

VtcGroupsBindingsAddV0_1MemberAction.description: What a member of a community-owned room may do there. `admin` is not among them: minting epochs, admitting and removing members are the community's, as the room's owner, and are exercised through the vtc/rooms/community/* tasks rather than by any member's credential. `curate` is not implied by `write`.

VtcGroupsBindingsAddV0_1MemberActions.description: The actions granted, at least one. An empty list confers nothing rather than everything, and a schema that allowed it would make the more dangerous reading available to a careless consumer.

VtcGroupsBindingsAddV0_1Payload.description: Bind a group to a community room, so its members are offered admission, or to a grant set or role's capabilities, which the community provisions into members' access-control entries with the group as their source. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

reason.description: Why, recorded with the change and shown to anyone who must approve it.

VtcGroupsBindingsAddV0_1ResourceQualifie.description: Opaque qualifier naming the part of the maintainer's resources a capability applies to (e.g. `git-ns:github.com/acme`, `git-repo:github.com/acme/r#4211`, `policy:join`). Its grammar and containment rule are the maintainer's: a qualified capability covers the named resource and the resources inside it. A qualifier MUST NOT be read as widening the entry's act scope.

VtcGroupsBindingsAddV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/groups/bindings/add/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/groups/bindings/add/0.1#response.

VtcGroupsBindingsAddV0_1RoleBindingSpec.description: A grant set by reference: the capability ceiling of a defined role, conferred as resource grants exactly as a `grants` binding confers its list. It never assigns the role itself — an entry's administrative role and its community role stay direct assignments.

VtcGroupsBindingsAddV0_1RoleName.description: A role identifier: lowercase, hyphen-separated, at most 64 characters. Compared by exact string equality. It is the value an AclEntry 0.2 carries in `role`.

VtcGroupsBindingsAddV0_1RoomBindingSpec.description: Links a room the community owns to the group: joining the group offers the member admission to the room with `actions`, valid for `validFor`, renewed while they stay in the group (collected with vtc/rooms/offers/list at 0.3 or later); leaving removes them unless another source still covers them.

validFor.description: How long each admission's authority runs, as an ISO 8601 duration in whole days (`P365D`). The community renews it while the member stays in the group.

VtcGroupsBindingsListV0_1Capability.description: Opaque identifier of one administrative power in the maintainer's capability registry — lowercase dot-separated segments (e.g. `keys.sign`, `vtc.roles.assign`, `git.repo.manage`). A consumer MUST NOT treat a capability it does not recognise as granted.

VtcGroupsBindingsListV0_1CapabilityRef.description: A capability, optionally qualified by a resource. Used where a capability is named but not granted — a role's ceiling, a role's approve ceiling, an entry's approvable capabilities. An unqualified reference covers every resource of the capability's kind.

VtcGroupsBindingsListV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcGroupsBindingsListV0_1GrantsBindingSp.description: A grant set the group confers: each capability is written onto every member's access-control entry as a resource grant whose source is the group, bounded by the member's role ceiling and by the binder's own holdings.

state.description: `pending`: waiting for the consent the community requires. `active`: in force; the community's reconciler keeps members' admissions and grants in line with it. `removing`: being withdrawn; the reconciler is removing what only this binding provided.

VtcGroupsBindingsListV0_1GroupId.description: Opaque identifier of a community group: `grp_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random and community-scoped; not the group's DID.

VtcGroupsBindingsListV0_1MemberAction.description: What a member of a community-owned room may do there. `admin` is not among them: minting epochs, admitting and removing members are the community's, as the room's owner, and are exercised through the vtc/rooms/community/* tasks rather than by any member's credential. `curate` is not implied by `write`.

VtcGroupsBindingsListV0_1MemberActions.description: The actions granted, at least one. An empty list confers nothing rather than everything, and a schema that allowed it would make the more dangerous reading available to a careless consumer.

VtcGroupsBindingsListV0_1Payload.description: A group manager or administrator lists what a group is bound to: the rooms its members are admitted to and the grants it confers. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

VtcGroupsBindingsListV0_1ResourceQualifi.description: Opaque qualifier naming the part of the maintainer's resources a capability applies to (e.g. `git-ns:github.com/acme`, `git-repo:github.com/acme/r#4211`, `policy:join`). Its grammar and containment rule are the maintainer's: a qualified capability covers the named resource and the resources inside it. A qualifier MUST NOT be read as widening the entry's act scope.

VtcGroupsBindingsListV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/groups/bindings/list/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/groups/bindings/list/0.1#response.

VtcGroupsBindingsListV0_1RoleBindingSpec.description: A grant set by reference: the capability ceiling of a defined role, conferred as resource grants exactly as a `grants` binding confers its list. VtcGroupsBindingsRemoveV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcGroupsBindingsRemoveV0_1GroupId.description: Opaque identifier of a community group: `grp_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random and community-scoped; not the group's DID.

VtcGroupsBindingsRemoveV0_1Payload.description: Remove a group's binding: members lose the room admission or grants it provided, unless another source still provides them. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

reason.description: Why, recorded with the change and shown to anyone who must approve it.

VtcGroupsBindingsRemoveV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/groups/bindings/remove/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/groups/bindings/remove/0.1#response.

state.description: `removed`: done. `removing`: the reconciler is withdrawing what only this binding provided. `pending`: a reduction of authority the community is holding on its terms.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1DynamicRule.description: A dynamic group's membership rule: a member belongs when every condition holds and they have not opted out. The community evaluates it under its `groups` policy and recomputes membership whenever a fact it reads changes, always excluding opted-out entries.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1EntryId.description: Opaque identifier of one directory entry: `dir_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random, scoped to one community, and stable for the life of the membership — it survives a rotation of the member's DID, which is why groups, notes and cards are keyed by it. It MUST NOT be derived from, and MUST NOT reveal, any DID of the member, and the same person's entries in two communities MUST NOT share one. Compared by exact string equality.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1FieldKey.description: Identifier of a directory field. A key with no `.` is a BASE field, the same in every community: `displayName`, `nickname`, `avatar`, `pronouns`, `bio`, `links` (written by the member) and `role`, `joinedAt`, `did`, `personhood` (derived from the community's own records, never stored on a card). A community-defined field MUST use a reverse-DNS key (`org.example.employer`), so a base key never collides with one, and a key is never reused with a different meaning once defined.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1Group.description: A community group, as a caller who may see it sees it. Members a caller may not see are absent: `memberCount` only to those who may see the group's members, `managers` and `credentialAuthorityValidUntil` only to its managers.

carriesAuthority.description: `true` while the group has a `grants` or `role` binding. Such a group is `static` and `closed` for as long as it does.

credentialAuthorityValidUntil.description: When the community's authorization credential to the group expires. The community renews it well before.

groupDid.description: The group's own DID, minted by the community's VTA for this group alone. It issues the group's membership credentials. Its DID document carries no name or description.

issuesCredentials.description: Whether the group's DID issues its members a membership credential. Default true.

managers.description: Entries holding `vtc.groups.manage` qualified to this group, read from the access-control list. Informational: managers are appointed by an access-control grant (vtc/groups/managers/add), never by this record.

memberCount.description: Active members. Only to callers who may see the member list.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1GroupAudience.description: Who may see something about a group, narrowest first. `admins`: holders of `vtc.groups.manage` for the group (unqualified, or qualified `group:<groupId>`). `groupMembers`: the group's own members, and its managers. `members`: every active member of the community.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1GroupDescription.description: What the group is for. Plain text; a reader MUST NOT treat it as instructions. Same placement rules as `GroupName`.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1GroupId.description: Opaque identifier of a community group: `grp_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random and community-scoped; not the group's DID.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1GroupKind.description: `static`: membership is explicit — added, joined, or granted on request. `dynamic`: membership is computed from `rule` over verified facts only; nobody is added by hand, but a member may opt out (vtc/groups/leave), an exclusion the rule cannot override, and undo it (vtc/groups/join). A dynamic group never confers authority. Fixed for the group's life.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1GroupName.description: The group's name, shown to those who may see the group. The community's own record: never in the group's DID document or its credentials' subject beyond the group's DID. Plain text.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1JoinPolicy.description: How a member enters a static group by themselves. `closed`: only a manager adds them. `request`: a member asks and a manager decides. `open`: a member joins at once, subject to the community's `groups` policy. A group carrying authority is always `closed`.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1Payload.description: An administrator creates a community group: the community's VTA mints the group's own DID and, where it issues credentials, the community authorises it to issue membership credentials; the group is recorded only afterwards. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

issuesCredentials.description: Whether the group's DID issues its members a membership credential. Absent: true.

reason.description: Why, recorded with the change and shown to anyone who must approve it.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/groups/create/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/groups/create/0.1#response.

VtcGroupsCreateV0_1RuleCondition.description: One test over a verified fact about a member. `fact: role` tests the member's community role; `fact: field` tests an `admin`- or `credential`-sourced directory field named by `field`; `fact: personhood` tests whether a personhood assertion is on file; `fact: joinedAt` tests when they joined. A rule never reads a self-asserted (`member`-sourced) field: a member must not be able to join a group by editing their card.

op.description: `equals` compares with `value`; `oneOf` with any of `values`; `exists` needs neither; `before` and `after` compare a date fact with `value`.

VtcGroupsDeleteV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcGroupsDeleteV0_1GroupId.description: Opaque identifier of a community group: `grp_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random and community-scoped; not the group's DID.

VtcGroupsDeleteV0_1Payload.description: A group manager deletes a group: its bindings are withdrawn first, its members' credential renewal stops and its authorization credential is revoked, and only then is the group removed. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

reason.description: Why, recorded with the change and shown to anyone who must approve it.

VtcGroupsDeleteV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/groups/delete/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/groups/delete/0.1#response.

state.description: `deleted`: done. `deleting`: the group no longer admits anyone and its bindings are being withdrawn; it disappears when they are.

VtcGroupsJoinV0_1CardBlobRef.description: A content-addressed image held in the community's blob store — an avatar or an `image` field. At most 256 KiB, images only, re-encoded by the community on upload (vtc/directory/images/upload: metadata stripped, dimensions capped) so its digest does not link the member across communities. A viewer reads the bytes with vtc/directory/images/get, which answers only where the same projection shows the value. `url` and `urlExpiresAt` MAY appear in a projection: a short-lived URL the community checks against the same projection, so a member-only image is never a public URL. A community that does not offer one leaves both out.

mediaType.description: Media type of the stored bytes.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the stored, re-encoded bytes.

size.description: Size in bytes of the stored bytes.

url.description: Projection only: a URL the viewer can fetch the image from until `urlExpiresAt`.

VtcGroupsJoinV0_1EntryFields.description: The fields of one entry that a particular viewer may see, keyed by field: the intersection of the member's visibility, the community's ceiling and policy, plus any derived fields that intersection admits. A withheld field is ABSENT, never null.

VtcGroupsJoinV0_1EntryId.description: Opaque identifier of one directory entry: `dir_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. A community-defined field MUST use a reverse-DNS key (`org.example.employer`), so a base key never collides with one, and a key is never reused with a different meaning once defined.

VtcGroupsJoinV0_1FieldValue.description: The value of one field. Which shape a field takes is fixed by its definition's `type`: text-like types (`text`, `longText`, `url`, `email`, `phone`, `enum`, `date` as YYYY-MM-DD, `country` as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, `did`) are strings; `multiEnum` and the base field `links` are arrays of strings; `image` and the base field `avatar` are a `CardBlobRef`; `claim` is a `VerifiedValue`; the derived base field `personhood` is a boolean.

VtcGroupsJoinV0_1GroupCredentialId.description: Identifier (`id`) of a group membership credential issued to a member. Each renewal issues a new credential with a new identifier. Validity is the community's setting; a community SHOULD default to 30 days, renewed when 10 days remain.

VtcGroupsJoinV0_1GroupId.description: Opaque identifier of a community group: `grp_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random and community-scoped; not the group's DID.

decidedBy.description: The manager who decided. Shown to managers only.

credentialId.description: The member's current group membership credential, or null when the group issues none.

credentialValidUntil.description: When the member's current group credential expires. Shown to the member themselves and to managers only.

state.description: `active`: a member. `pending`: an addition to a group carrying authority that is waiting for the consent the community requires for a grant.

VtcGroupsJoinV0_1JoinRequestMessage.description: An optional note from the member to the group's managers. Plain text.

VtcGroupsJoinV0_1MembershipSource.description: How the member came to be in the group. `added`: by a manager. `joined`: they joined an open group. `requestApproved`: a manager approved their request. `rule`: a dynamic group's rule admits them.

VtcGroupsJoinV0_1Payload.description: A member joins an open group at once, or asks to join a group that takes requests; where the group issues credentials, they are offered a membership credential issued by the group's DID. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

VtcGroupsJoinV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/groups/join/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/groups/join/0.1#response.

credentialId.description: The membership credential offered, or null when the group issues none or the outcome is `requested`.

outcome.description: `joined`: a member now. `requested`: a request awaits a manager. `optOutWithdrawn`: the caller's opt-out of a dynamic group is undone, but its rule does not admit them now; they become a member when it does.

VtcGroupsJoinV0_1VerifiedValue.description: The value of a `credential`-sourced field: a claim the member disclosed from a credential they presented, with the issuer that attests it. A verified value always names its issuer, and a self-asserted value is never shaped as one. The community keeps only the disclosed claim and these facts about it — never the presentation.

credentialType.description: The most specific `type` of the credential the claim came from.

issuer.description: DID of the credential's issuer, shown as the field's verification badge.

validUntil.description: When the credential expires, where it does. The community withdraws the value once it passes.

verifiedAt.description: When the community verified the presentation.

VtcGroupsLeaveV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcGroupsLeaveV0_1GroupId.description: Opaque identifier of a community group: `grp_` followed by 16 to 64 base64url characters. Random and community-scoped; not the group's DID.

VtcGroupsLeaveV0_1Payload.description: A member leaves a static group, opts out of a dynamic one, or withdraws a pending request to join: renewal of their group credential stops, and what only the group provided is withdrawn. The outer document members are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

VtcGroupsLeaveV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/groups/leave/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/groups/leave/0.1#response.

credentialValidUntil.description: When the member's last group credential lapses; renewal has stopped. Null when they held none.

state.description: `left`: out of a static group. `optedOut`: out of a dynamic group, and kept out whatever its rule says until the member joins again. `requestWithdrawn`: a pending request is withdrawn. `pending`: leaving a group carrying authority, which the community executes as a reduction of the member's own authority on its terms.

issuesCredentials.description: Turning it off stops issuing and renewing members' credentials; those issued lapse at their expiry.

reason.description: Why, recorded with the change and shown to anyone who must approve it.

VtcGroupsUpdateV0_1Response.description: The success response to a vtc/groups/update/0.1 request. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/groups/update/0.1#response.

VtcGroupsUpdateV0_1RuleCondition.description: One test over a verified fact about a member. `fact: role` tests the member's community role; `fact: field` tests an `admin`- or `credential`-sourced directory field named by `field`; `fact: personhood` tests whether a personhood assertion is on file; `fact: joinedAt` tests when they joined. A rule never reads a self-asserted (`member`-sourced) field: a member must not be able to join a group by editing their card.

op.description: `equals` compares with `value`; `oneOf` with any of `values`; `exists` needs neither; `before` and `after` compare a date fact with `value`.

VtcInvitationsDeliverV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcInvitationsDeliverV0_1Payload.description: Deliver an issued invitation to the DID it admits: push an offer to that DID, or return the offer for a QR code. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

channel.description: `message`: the community sends a `credential-exchange/offer` to the invited DID over a transport that DID advertises. `offer`: the community returns the offer, for the inviter to hand over out of band — typically as a QR code.

id.description: Identifier of the invitation to deliver, as `vtc/invitations/list` reports it.

expiresAt.description: When this delivery's offer lapses. Never later than the invitation's own expiry.

offer.description: Present exactly when `channel` is `offer`: an OID4VCI Credential Offer object, carried verbatim, whose pre-authorized code redeems only for the invited DID. Its members are OID4VCI's and are deliberately not re-specified here.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_3ClaimType.description:
The vocabulary token naming what a value IS — `name.legal`, `phone.mobile`, `address.postal`, `person.birthDate`. Dotted, most-general segment first, so that a consumer with no knowledge of the specific token can still group by its prefix.

The token is the maintainer's own; no external vocabulary is primary. External vocabularies (vCard/jCard, OIDC standard claims, schema.org) are mappings applied at PRESENTATION by a renderer, not at rest, so that a query written in any of them can be matched without the store having to live inside any one of them.

The `x:` prefix is an open extension namespace and is not decoration. The closest prior art — Windows CardSpace's self-issued card — supported exactly fifteen predefined claim types with no extensibility, and that is the specific way it failed the requirement a holder actually has. An `x:` attribute stores, composes, binds and discloses exactly like a known one; it renders generically and matches only an explicit query.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_3CommunityBran.description: OPTIONAL. How the community asks to be shown to a prospective applicant: a name, an accent colour and a logo. Presentation only, self-asserted and unverified — `communityDid` identifies the community, never `branding`. Not part of any criterion, so not covered by a `requirementsDigest`. Every member is optional.

accentColor.description: An sRGB colour as `#rrggbb`, compared case-insensitively. A community SHOULD write it in lower case.

displayName.description: The community's name as it asks to be shown.

logoUrl.description: An https URL of the community's logo. Fetched by the client, so an untrusted image from wherever it points.

admission.description: How the community decides a submission that meets this criterion. `automatic`: it admits the applicant without a person deciding. `review`: it refers the submission to an administrator, who decides.

credentialIssuers.description: Whose credentials meet `presentationDefinition`: `community` (this community's own), `recognised` (this community's, or a community it recognises), or `any` (any issuer whose credential verifies). Present exactly when `presentationDefinition` is.

description.description: Plain-language summary of the criterion, authored by the community and shown to prospective applicants. Informative: where it and `vetting` disagree, `vetting` governs.

invitationRequired.description: True: the criterion is met only by a submission carrying a valid, unconsumed invitation this community issued to the applicant.

presentationDefinition.description: The credentials an applicant must present for this criterion (opaque here). Absent: the criterion requires no credential.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_3DigestMultiba.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_3Duration.description: An ISO 8601 duration in weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds only (e.g. `P120D`, `P2W`, `P1DT12H`, `PT15M`). Years and months are refused: their length depends on the calendar, and an age limit that means different things on different days is not a limit.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_3Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_3ExtCritical.description:
Names the `ext` namespaces a consumer MUST understand or refuse, per SPEC.md §4.5.1.

Every entry MUST be an immediate key of the sibling `ext` object at the same level; an entry naming an absent namespace is non-conforming and the consumer rejects the document with `malformedRequest`. A consumer that does not recognize a namespace named here MUST NOT process the document as though the namespace were absent, and rejects it with `unsupportedExtension` — the exception to the rule that unrecognized namespaces are ignored.

A producer marks a namespace only where the document's meaning depends on it. Marking one that merely carries a hint or an annotation turns every consumer that has not implemented it into a failure where it would otherwise have interoperated. JSON Schema cannot check either of those rules: that an entry names a present namespace is checkable only against the sibling `ext`, and whether a namespace is load-bearing is not a schema question at all. Both are consumer-side checks.

purpose.description: Why the community asks, in words shown to the applicant before they disclose.

required.description: False for an attribute the applicant may decline. A submission missing a required one is refused with vtc/join-requests/submit:attributesMissing.

type.description: A claim-type token from the persona claim-type registry (persona/_shared/0.1/CLAIM-TYPES.md) — `name.display`, `address.country` — or an `x:` extension token.

requestedAttributes.description: What the community asks an applicant to tell it about themselves, as claim types — never values. Answered in persona terms: the applicant's agent discloses those attributes from the face the applicant chooses, and they arrive on vtc/join-requests/submit as `attributes`. SELF-ASSERTED: a community MUST NOT describe an answer as verified, and MUST NOT make a decision that assumes it is. Outside every criterion, so no `requirementsDigest` covers it. Absent when the community asks nothing.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_3VettingDocume.description: A class of documentation, named in lowerCamelCase. Open rather than enumerated, because what documentation a vetter accepts is each vetter's own choice. Well-known values: `passport`, `nationalId`, `driverLicence`, and `none` — the vetter will attest without a document, which is the `priorAcquaintance` case. Only the class ever travels — never a document number, an image, an issuing authority or an expiry date. `none` states a policy (what a vetter accepts); a record of what was relied on expresses 'no document' as an empty list instead.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_3VettingMethod.description: How the vetter established that the person they checked is the person controlling the applicant's DID. `inPerson` — both people were physically together. `video` — a live, two-way video call. `priorAcquaintance` — the vetter has known or worked with this person over a period, and attests from that knowledge rather than from a document. A method is a description of what happened, not an assurance level: which methods count, and how many of each, is community policy.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_3VettingRelati.description: The vetter's own declaration of how they relate to the applicant. Declared, not verified: it exists so community policy can cap how much evidence comes from people close to the applicant, and a false declaration is the vetter's attributable act.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_3VettingRequir.description: What identity-vetting evidence a criterion needs, beyond what a presentation-definition can express: distinct eligible vetters, per-method floors, independence caps. Every number is the community's own policy. This schema supplies no defaults — an absent optional member means the community imposes no constraint of that kind, never that some protocol value applies. Deliberately open: a consumer MUST ignore members it does not recognise, so a community publishing a newer shape does not make an older client unable to read the rest. Durations: `maxStatementAge` — a statement older than this at decision time does not count (absent: no limit beyond the statement's own validity); `decisionSla` — how long after submission the community undertakes to decide, including on a referred application; `requirementsGrace` — how long an application started under an earlier `requirementsDigest` is still evaluated under that version.

acceptedDocumentClasses.description: Documentation a statement must have relied on in order to count. Absent — the expected case — means each vetter decides what documentation they accept, including none for prior acquaintance, and the community counts what they attest.

acceptedMethods.description: Methods whose statements count at all.

eligibleVetters.description: How a vetter's eligibility is established.

role.description: The role a statement's issuer must hold, matched as the action `role:<role>` in a Verifiable Authority Credential (`AuthorityCredential`) the community issued to that issuer, whose `authority.scope` is the community's DID (see `vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1`). A statement counts only if its issuer holds such a credential.

governanceFrameworkUrl.description: Where the community's vetting governance — including the attestation text vetters sign — is published.

independence.description: Caps on how much evidence may come from people close to the applicant. Absent: no caps.

maxByDeclaredRelationship.description: The most counted statements that may come from vetters declaring each relationship — e.g. `{ "family": 0 }`.

requireConsistentIdentityCommitment.description: When true, every counted statement must carry the same identity commitment — all vetters verified the same claimed identity. Absent: false.

invitation.description: Whether an invitation credential must accompany the statements at submission (`required`), may (`optional`), or plays no part (`none`). Absent: the presentation-definition alone governs.

minByMethod.description: Per-method floors within `minStatements` — e.g. `{ "inPerson": 1 }`. Every method named MUST also be in `acceptedMethods`. Absent: no method floor.

minStatements.description: How many counted statements are needed, counting each vetter once however many DIDs they hold.

optionalClaims.description: Claim types an applicant MAY add to the card and a vetter MAY verify. They never affect whether a statement counts.

requiredClaims.description: Claim types the applicant's Vetting Card must carry, which the identity commitment is computed over, and which a counted statement must list as verified. Absent: none.

statementType.description: The predicate IRI a counted vetting statement carries in `credentialSubject.predicate` — `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`, the DTG VSC registry's identity-vetting predicate, or a predicate in a namespace the community controls — registered as one the community accepts via vtc/endorsement-types/register. A statement under any other predicate does not count.

version.description: Version of this requirements object's shape. `0.1` for the members defined here.

externalCards.description: Whether a member may publish a card beyond the community: their `public` values, signed by them, offered through the community's trust registry. Always the member's own choice, and off on a new card. False where the community cannot publish external cards.

fields.description: Every active field, base and community-defined, in display order. A base field the community has disabled is absent, which is how a reader learns it is not collected.

facet.description: Whether members may filter on the field and see counts by its values. Absent: false.

searchable.description: Whether a member's search may match the field, within what the searcher may see.

A community-defined field MUST use a reverse-DNS key (`org.example.employer`), so a base key never collides with one, and a key is never reused with a different meaning once defined.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_4FieldLabel.description: What readers see as the field's name. Plain text.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_4FieldSource.description: Who writes the value. `member`: self-asserted, through vtc/directory/card/update. `admin`: asserted by the community through vtc/directory/card/assert; the member reads it and cannot change it. `credential`: a claim the member discloses from a credential through vtc/directory/card/present, badged with its issuer. `derived`: a base field read from the community's own records (`role`, `joinedAt`, `did`, `personhood`) and never stored on a card. Each source is written only through its own path.

credentialValidity.description: How long each group membership credential is valid for, as an ISO 8601 duration in weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds (`P30D`). It is renewed while the member stays in the group, and a credential already issued stays valid until it expires even after its holder leaves.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_4Introductions.description: Who may ask the community to introduce them to this member. `anyone`: any active member who can find the entry. `groups`: only members who share a community group with them. `connections`: only members holding an attributed, in-force verified relationship with them. `off`: nobody. A refused introduction is never reported to its sender.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_4Listing.description: Whether members can find the entry. `listed`: it appears when members browse. `findable`: it does not appear when browsing, but a search that matches it under `search` returns it. `hidden`: no member finds it by browsing or searching; administrators still see it, and members who share a group that shows its members see it in that group's member list.

VtcJoinRequestsManifestV0_4NewCardDefaul.description: The discoverability a card has when the community creates it, before its member chooses. A new card is never published beyond the community (VTI-DIR-042), so there is no member for that here: `externalCards` says whether the member may turn it on.

VtcMembersCredentialsV0_1Response.description: The documents the community holds for this member. Every credential member is optional; absent means the community holds no such document, which is a real answer rather than a failure.

memberVmcBound.description: Whether the acknowledgement's digest was verified against the grant. REQUIRED so that 'not verified' is stated rather than inferred from silence.
