memberVmcReceivedAt.description: When the acknowledgement arrived. Paired with `memberVmc`; a maintainer must not send one without the other.

membershipCredential.description: The community-issued Verifiable Membership Credential — the grant. A verifiable credential, carried verbatim and opaque to this schema. Maintainers must not re-serialise it — the bytes carry a proof over themselves. Matches the `vrcJsonld` idiom in vtc/relationships/list/0.2.

roleCredential.description: The role credential: a community-issued Verifiable Authority Credential (`AuthorityCredential`) conferring `role:<name>` at the community's DID. A verifiable credential, carried verbatim and opaque to this schema. Maintainers must not re-serialise it — the bytes carry a proof over themselves. Matches the `vrcJsonld` idiom in vtc/relationships/list/0.2.

VtcRegistryRecordsListV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

authorized.description: Present on authorization records: whether the action+resource authorization is confirmed. Absent on other record types — absent is not `false`.

entityId.description: The entity the record is about.

recognized.description: Present on recognition records: whether the action+resource is recognised. Absent on other record types — absent is not `false`.

recordType.description: Record discriminator, as the trust registry states it.

items.description: The matching records, in the maintainer's stable enumeration order.

nextCursor.description: Continuation token for the next page, or null when this is the last.

VtcRegistryRecordsListV0_1Source.description: `registry` enumerates the trust registry itself; `local` enumerates the community's own record of what it published. They are different questions and a consumer MUST NOT treat one as a cache of the other.

VtcRegistrySyncJobsDiscardV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

memberDid.description: The member whose pending change was dropped. Returned because the caller is discarding by identifier and this names what it actually cost.

VtcRegistrySyncJobsListV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

attempts.description: Attempts made so far. `1` on a failed job means the registry answered and refused; a value at the maintainer's retry ceiling means it never answered.

jobId.description: Identifier of the queued job. The handle `vtc/registry/sync-jobs/retry` and `.../discard` take.

lastError.description: The registry's last answer, verbatim. Diagnostic prose for an operator; a consumer MUST NOT parse it.

memberDid.description: The member whose registry record the job carries. In the clear, because an operator holding a hash cannot tell who stopped publishing.

nextAttemptAt.description: When it is next due. Null on a failed job: nothing is scheduled.

purgeDueAt.description: When the maintainer's retention sweep will delete this row. A deadline, not a fix — the member stays unpublished.

VtcRegistrySyncJobsListV0_1Kind.description: Which mutation the job carries to the registry.

nextCursor.description: Continuation token for the next page, or null when this is the last.

VtcRegistrySyncJobsListV0_1State.description: `failed` is terminal: the reconciler has abandoned the job and will not retry it without an operator. `pending` and `inFlight` are moving on their own.

VtcRegistrySyncJobsRetryV0_2Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

from.description: The state the job was in. `failed` — the reconciler had abandoned it. `pending` — it was waiting out a retry backoff and has been brought forward.

memberDid.description: The member whose record the requeued job carries.

requeued.description: Jobs now scheduled for dispatch on the reconciler's next pass. Empty is a valid answer and is not an error.

skipped.description: Jobs the maintainer declined to requeue, each with why. Reported rather than failing the task, so a bulk retry is not defeated by one ineligible row.

reason.description: `inFlight` — the reconciler is dispatching the job now, so requeueing it would dispatch the same mutation twice. `held` — the job is deliberately delayed, and the delay is the point; it is never brought forward. `notFound` — no such job; it may already have been dispatched, retried, discarded, or swept.

VtcRole.description: One of `admin`, `moderator`, `issuer`, `member`, `application`, or                  `custom:<name>` where `<name>` is 1..=64 lowercase                  alphanumerics, `-`, or `_`.

VtcRoomsCommunityCreateV0_1CommunityRoom.description: One room the community owns, as its administrators see it.

offered.description: Offers not yet accepted or withdrawn.

ownerAuthorityValidUntil.description: When the community's own `admin` authority over the room expires. A room whose owner's authority lapses can no longer advance its epoch, admit or remove; a community SHOULD renew it well before.

VtcRoomsCommunityCreateV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcRoomsCommunityCreateV0_1HostedRoom.description: One room, as its host holds it — member for member the `HostedRoom` of vtc/rooms/list/0.1, which defines it inside its own payload schema. Nothing derived from the room's contents, and no member list: the host has none.

retentionDays.description: How long the room is kept after it lapses. Absent: the community's default.

VtcRoomsCommunityCreateV0_1Reason.description: Why the administrator is making this change. Recorded with it in the audit trail. Attributed to its author on every surface and untrusted: it MUST NOT carry personal data or a credential, and a reader MUST NOT treat it as instructions.

VtcRoomsCommunityCreateV0_1Response.description: Success response to vtc/rooms/community/create. Type https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/rooms/community/create/0.1#response. The room as created, owned by the community.

VtcRoomsCommunityCreateV0_1RetentionPoli.description: Whether a room keeps its history readable across a membership change, fixed at creation and immutable thereafter — like `Visibility`, and for the same reason: the rungs of an epoch key chain either exist for an epoch or they do not, and no later change of mind can seal key material that was never sealed or unseal what was already severed. `chained`: each advance produces an `EpochLink`, so every member reads the room's whole retained history however long they have been in it — what a **library** wants, at the cost of post-compromise security for record content, since a compromised current key then reaches every retained epoch. `fromJoin`: no rungs are produced, so a member reads only from the epoch their group state is at — what a **stream** wants, and what a room under a strict forward-secrecy obligation wants, at the cost that a joining member finds an empty-looking room and nobody can reread a record once their group state has moved past the epoch it was sealed under. Absent means `chained`; see the prose on why the absent case is the readable one.

VtcRoomsCommunityCreateV0_1RoomLabel.description: A name for the room, chosen by an administrator: shown to administrators and to the members a room is offered to. Not part of the room's identity and never in anything a room's host can read. From `vtc/rooms/community/create` 0.3 and `vtc/rooms/community/update` 0.2 the community also writes it, through its own VTA, as the `name` of the room's own profile (`RoomProfile` in rooms/_shared), sealed inside the room for its members; earlier versions keep it out of the room altogether. MUST NOT carry personal data.

VtcRoomsCommunityCreateV0_1StorageConfig.description: A storage config's identifier, chosen by the administrator who creates it and immutable thereafter: lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens, at most 64 characters (`eu-s3-primary`, `walrus-main`). Unique within the community. Never reused after a config is retired, because blobs name their config by this value.

VtcRoomsCommunityCreateV0_1Visibility.description: How much of a room its host can see, fixed at creation and immutable thereafter. `open`: records are cleartext, searchable and fully audited. `attributed`: record content is sealed, and the host still learns which member acted. `private`: content is sealed and membership is presented in zero knowledge, so the host verifies that a member acted without learning which. Immutable because a downgrade cannot un-see cleartext and an upgrade would protect only what came after while presenting as though it protected everything.

VtcRoomsCommunityCreateV0_2CommunityRoom.description: What vtc/rooms/community/{create,get,list}/0.2 and vtc/rooms/community/update/0.1 return: `CommunityRoom` plus the details an administrator keeps track of a room by — `description`, `tags`, and who last changed them and when. A separate definition, not a change to `CommunityRoom`, so that the 0.1 versions of those tasks keep the exact shape they published. The room's creation is `room.createdAt` and `createdBy`.

detailsUpdatedAt.description: When `label`, `description` or `tags` last changed. Absent until the first change after creation. Distinct from `room.updatedAt`, which is the host record's and moves with the room's epoch and lifecycle.

detailsUpdatedBy.description: The administrator who made that change. Present exactly when `detailsUpdatedAt` is. The earlier values and who set them are in the community's audit trail, not here.

ownerAuthorityValidUntil.description: When the community's own `admin` authority over the room expires. A room whose owner's authority lapses can no longer advance its epoch, admit or remove; a community SHOULD renew it well before.

VtcRoomsCommunityListV0_1RetentionPolicy.description: Whether a room keeps its history readable across a membership change, fixed at creation and immutable thereafter — like `Visibility`, and for the same reason: the rungs of an epoch key chain either exist for an epoch or they do not, and no later change of mind can seal key material that was never sealed or unseal what was already severed. `chained`: each advance produces an `EpochLink`, so every member reads the room's whole retained history however long they have been in it — what a **library** wants, at the cost of post-compromise security for record content, since a compromised current key then reaches every retained epoch. `fromJoin`: no rungs are produced, so a member reads only from the epoch their group state is at — what a **stream** wants, and what a room under a strict forward-secrecy obligation wants, at the cost that a joining member finds an empty-looking room and nobody can reread a record once their group state has moved past the epoch it was sealed under. VtcRoomsCommunityMembersRemoveV0_2Digest.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.

From `vtc/rooms/community/create` 0.3 and `vtc/rooms/community/update` 0.2 the community also writes it, through its own VTA, as the `name` of the room's own profile (`RoomProfile` in rooms/_shared), sealed inside the room for its members; earlier versions keep it out of the room altogether. MUST NOT carry personal data.

VtcRoomsCommunityUpdateV0_2RoomTag.description: A short identifier an administrator files a community-owned room under — `board`, `working-group`, `finance` — so the room list can be filtered. Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. Owner-side tracking metadata for holders of `vtc.rooms.manage` only: never shown to members, never sent on the room's host path, and it confers nothing.

VtcRoomsCommunityUpdateV0_2RoomTags.description: The room's tags, at most eight, as a set: order carries no meaning. An empty list means the room has none — a tag grants nothing, so empty has no more dangerous reading.

VtcRoomsCommunityUpdateV0_2StorageConfig.description: A storage config's identifier, chosen by the administrator who creates it and immutable thereafter: lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens, at most 64 characters (`eu-s3-primary`, `walrus-main`). Unique within the community. Never reused after a config is retired, because blobs name their config by this value.

VtcRoomsCommunityUpdateV0_2Visibility.description: How much of a room its host can see, fixed at creation and immutable thereafter. `open`: records are cleartext, searchable and fully audited. `attributed`: record content is sealed, and the host still learns which member acted. `private`: content is sealed and membership is presented in zero knowledge, so the host verifies that a member acted without learning which. Immutable because a downgrade cannot un-see cleartext and an upgrade would protect only what came after while presenting as though it protected everything.

VtcRoomsGetV0_1ConfigHoldings.description: A config holding some of this room's blobs, other than the one it is assigned to.

VtcRoomsGetV0_1EffectiveLimits.description: The limits a room is enforced against now, with where each scope's came from.

hostCeilingBytes.description: The host-wide largest-file ceiling, which no room or member limit can exceed.

VtcRoomsGetV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcRoomsGetV0_1HostedRoom.description: One room, as its host holds it — member for member the `HostedRoom` of vtc/rooms/list/0.1, which defines it inside its own payload schema. Nothing derived from the room's contents, and no member list: the host has none.

VtcRoomsGetV0_1LimitSource.description: Where an effective limit came from. `policy`: the community's rooms policy at the room's creation. `override`: an administrator's vtc/rooms/limits/set. `default`: the community's configured defaults, where neither applies. The host-wide ceiling bounds all three.

VtcRoomsGetV0_1MigrationProgress.description: Progress of the room's migration, as vtc/rooms/storage/migrate reports it.

state.description: `paused`: halted by a capacity or backend failure and resumable by issuing vtc/rooms/storage/migrate again. `failed`: halted on a blob whose copy did not verify; the blob stays where it was.

largestBlobs.description: The room's largest committed blobs, by size only.

membersWithUsage.description: On an `attributed` room only: how many members have added files. Absent on `open` and `private` rooms.

orphans.description: Blobs no record names, awaiting deletion after the grace window.

VtcRoomsGetV0_1RetentionPolicy.description: Whether a room keeps its history readable across a membership change, fixed at creation and immutable thereafter — like `Visibility`, and for the same reason: the rungs of an epoch key chain either exist for an epoch or they do not, and no later change of mind can seal key material that was never sealed or unseal what was already severed. `chained`: each advance produces an `EpochLink`, so every member reads the room's whole retained history however long they have been in it — what a **library** wants, at the cost of post-compromise security for record content, since a compromised current key then reaches every retained epoch. `fromJoin`: no rungs are produced, so a member reads only from the epoch their group state is at — what a **stream** wants, and what a room under a strict forward-secrecy obligation wants, at the cost that a joining member finds an empty-looking room and nobody can reread a record once their group state has moved past the epoch it was sealed under. Absent means `chained`; see the prose on why the absent case is the readable one.

VtcRoomsGetV0_1RoomLimits.description: How much a host is willing to store for one room, at the room and per member. A hosting decision, set by the host and never by anything in the room's credentials. An upload must fit every scope at once: the object against the smallest `maxFileBytes` that applies, and the member and the room with the file added.

filesEnabled.description: False refuses every rooms/blobs/* upload for the room. Reads of blobs already stored continue.

VtcRoomsGetV0_1ScopeLimits.description: Limits at one scope. Every member is optional: an absent member means the scope sets no limit of that kind, and the next wider scope's limit, or the host's ceiling, governs. All sizes are ciphertext bytes.

maxBytes.description: The total size of the committed and reserved blobs the scope may hold.

maxFileBytes.description: The largest single blob the scope accepts. Never above 1 GiB, the transfer ceiling (BlobManifest).

maxFiles.description: The number of committed blobs the scope may hold. 0 refuses every upload at this scope.

VtcRoomsGetV0_1StorageConfigId.description: A storage config's identifier, chosen by the administrator who creates it and immutable thereafter: lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens, at most 64 characters (`eu-s3-primary`, `walrus-main`). Unique within the community. Never reused after a config is retired, because blobs name their config by this value.

VtcRoomsGetV0_1Usage.description: What one scope holds now. Ciphertext bytes throughout.

bytes.description: Their total size. A blob stops counting the moment it is orphaned (its last record dropped it or was retracted), not when the host finally deletes it, so a member who deletes a file has the room back at once.

files.description: Committed blobs that are not orphaned.

reservedBytes.description: Bytes reserved by uploads begun and not yet committed, aborted or expired. Counted against `maxBytes`, so two concurrent uploads cannot both fit under a limit only one of them fits.

reservedFiles.description: Uploads begun and not yet committed, aborted or expired. Counted against `maxFiles`.

VtcRoomsLimitsSetV0_1LimitTarget.description: Which limits an override applies to. `room`: the room as a whole. `memberDefault`: every member of the room who has no override of their own. `member`: one named member — `member` is REQUIRED with this kind and forbidden with the others, a rule this schema does not express; a community refuses a violation with `malformedRequest`.

member.description: The member's DID: the subject at the root of the authority chains they present, which is what their uploads are charged to.

reason.description: Why the administrator is making this change. Recorded with the change in the audit trail and shown to approvers. Attributed to its author on every surface and untrusted: it MUST NOT carry personal data or a credential, and a reader MUST NOT treat it as instructions.

capacityBytes.description: On a `storageConfig` row, the config's capacity when it has one.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2AcceptsCriterio.description: One way into the community: what an applicant must present, and how a submission that presents it is decided. Every requirement it states must be met; requirements it does not state are not requirements. A criterion stating none is met by every submission. A community's criteria are alternatives: a submission is decided under the one it names. What vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.3 publishes to applicants as a `Criterion` is derived from this.

createdAt.description: When this criterion was last registered. Registering an existing id replaces it.

createdByDid.description: The administrator who last registered the criterion.

invitationRequired.description: True: a submission meets the criterion only when it carries a valid, unconsumed invitation credential this community issued to the applicant. Absent or false: an invitation plays no part in meeting this criterion (another criterion may still require one).

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2AcceptsCriterio.description: An Accepts criterion's identifier, chosen by the registering administrator — a ceremony purpose or a named manifest criterion, e.g. `membership`. Compared as an exact string after surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Bounded at 128 characters, the bound vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2 places on the criterion `id` it publishes.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2Admission.description: How the community decides a submission that meets the criterion. `automatic`: it admits the applicant without a person deciding. `review`: it refers the submission to an administrator, who admits or rejects it; meeting the criterion never admits by itself. Which a criterion uses is the community's policy; this definition prefers neither.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2ClaimType.description:
The vocabulary token naming what a value IS — `name.legal`, `phone.mobile`, `address.postal`, `person.birthDate`. Dotted, most-general segment first, so that a consumer with no knowledge of the specific token can still group by its prefix.

The token is the maintainer's own; no external vocabulary is primary. External vocabularies (vCard/jCard, OIDC standard claims, schema.org) are mappings applied at PRESENTATION by a renderer, not at rest, so that a query written in any of them can be matched without the store having to live inside any one of them.

The `x:` prefix is an open extension namespace and is not decoration. The closest prior art — Windows CardSpace's self-issued card — supported exactly fifteen predefined claim types with no extensibility, and that is the specific way it failed the requirement a holder actually has. An `x:` attribute stores, composes, binds and discloses exactly like a known one; it renders generically and matches only an explicit query.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2CredentialIssue.description: Whose credentials meet the criterion's `query`. `community`: only credentials this community issued. `recognised`: credentials this community issued, or issued by a community it recognises (vtc/recognition/check). `any`: any issuer whose credential verifies — the query's own constraints, including DCQL `trusted_authorities`, are then all that limits it. A credential that does not verify (signature, validity window, revocation) never meets a criterion, whichever value is chosen.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2CriterionDescri.description: Plain-language summary of the criterion, written by the registering administrator. Published to prospective applicants in the join manifest, and used as the `purpose` of the credential-exchange/query a join sends when the criterion has a `query` — so it is read by applicants and their agents, not only by administrators. Untrusted as a statement of the rule: where it and the criterion's other members disagree, those govern.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2DcqlQuery.description: An OpenID for Verifiable Presentations DCQL query, carried verbatim: per-credential `format`, `meta` type selector (`vct_values`) and requested `claims`. Defined by OID4VP and not re-specified here; snake_case member names are DCQL's own. The community parses it as DCQL and checks every type it references against the registry.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2Duration.description: An ISO 8601 duration in weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds only (e.g. `P120D`, `P2W`, `P1DT12H`, `PT15M`). Years and months are refused: their length depends on the calendar, and an age limit that means different things on different days is not a limit.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2ExtCritical.description:
Names the `ext` namespaces a consumer MUST understand or refuse, per SPEC.md §4.5.1.

Every entry MUST be an immediate key of the sibling `ext` object at the same level; an entry naming an absent namespace is non-conforming and the consumer rejects the document with `malformedRequest`. A consumer that does not recognize a namespace named here MUST NOT process the document as though the namespace were absent, and rejects it with `unsupportedExtension` — the exception to the rule that unrecognized namespaces are ignored.

A producer marks a namespace only where the document's meaning depends on it. Marking one that merely carries a hint or an annotation turns every consumer that has not implemented it into a failure where it would otherwise have interoperated. JSON Schema cannot check either of those rules: that an entry names a present namespace is checkable only against the sibling `ext`, and whether a namespace is load-bearing is not a schema question at all. Both are consumer-side checks.

nextCursor.description: Present when more criteria remain; pass it as `cursor`.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2VettingDocument.description: A class of documentation, named in lowerCamelCase. Open rather than enumerated, because what documentation a vetter accepts is each vetter's own choice. Well-known values: `passport`, `nationalId`, `driverLicence`, and `none` — the vetter will attest without a document, which is the `priorAcquaintance` case. Only the class ever travels — never a document number, an image, an issuing authority or an expiry date. `none` states a policy (what a vetter accepts); a record of what was relied on expresses 'no document' as an empty list instead.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2VettingMethod.description: How the vetter established that the person they checked is the person controlling the applicant's DID. `inPerson` — both people were physically together. `video` — a live, two-way video call. `priorAcquaintance` — the vetter has known or worked with this person over a period, and attests from that knowledge rather than from a document. A method is a description of what happened, not an assurance level: which methods count, and how many of each, is community policy.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2VettingRelation.description: The vetter's own declaration of how they relate to the applicant. Declared, not verified: it exists so community policy can cap how much evidence comes from people close to the applicant, and a false declaration is the vetter's attributable act.

VtcSchemasAcceptsListV0_2VettingRequirem.description: What identity-vetting evidence a criterion needs, beyond what a presentation-definition can express: distinct eligible vetters, per-method floors, independence caps. Every number is the community's own policy. This schema supplies no defaults — an absent optional member means the community imposes no constraint of that kind, never that some protocol value applies. Deliberately open: a consumer MUST ignore members it does not recognise, so a community publishing a newer shape does not make an older client unable to read the rest. Durations: `maxStatementAge` — a statement older than this at decision time does not count (absent: no limit beyond the statement's own validity); `decisionSla` — how long after submission the community undertakes to decide, including on a referred application; `requirementsGrace` — how long an application started under an earlier `requirementsDigest` is still evaluated under that version.

acceptedDocumentClasses.description: Documentation a statement must have relied on in order to count. Absent — the expected case — means each vetter decides what documentation they accept, including none for prior acquaintance, and the community counts what they attest.

acceptedMethods.description: Methods whose statements count at all.

eligibleVetters.description: How a vetter's eligibility is established.

role.description: The role a statement's issuer must hold, matched as the action `role:<role>` in a Verifiable Authority Credential (`AuthorityCredential`) the community issued to that issuer, whose `authority.scope` is the community's DID (see `vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1`). A statement counts only if its issuer holds such a credential.

governanceFrameworkUrl.description: Where the community's vetting governance — including the attestation text vetters sign — is published.

independence.description: Caps on how much evidence may come from people close to the applicant. Absent: no caps.

maxByDeclaredRelationship.description: The most counted statements that may come from vetters declaring each relationship — e.g. `{ "family": 0 }`.

requireConsistentIdentityCommitment.description: When true, every counted statement must carry the same identity commitment — all vetters verified the same claimed identity. Absent: false.

invitation.description: Whether an invitation credential must accompany the statements at submission (`required`), may (`optional`), or plays no part (`none`). Absent: the presentation-definition alone governs.

minByMethod.description: Per-method floors within `minStatements` — e.g. `{ "inPerson": 1 }`. Every method named MUST also be in `acceptedMethods`. Absent: no method floor.

minStatements.description: How many counted statements are needed, counting each vetter once however many DIDs they hold.

optionalClaims.description: Claim types an applicant MAY add to the card and a vetter MAY verify. They never affect whether a statement counts.

requiredClaims.description: Claim types the applicant's Vetting Card must carry, which the identity commitment is computed over, and which a counted statement must list as verified. Absent: none.

statementType.description: The predicate IRI a counted vetting statement carries in `credentialSubject.predicate` — `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`, the DTG VSC registry's identity-vetting predicate, or a predicate in a namespace the community controls — registered as one the community accepts via vtc/endorsement-types/register. A statement under any other predicate does not count.

version.description: Version of this requirements object's shape. `0.1` for the members defined here.

A method is a description of what happened, not an assurance level: which methods count, and how many of each, is community policy.

VtcSchemasAcceptsRegisterV0_2VettingRela.description: The vetter's own declaration of how they relate to the applicant. Declared, not verified: it exists so community policy can cap how much evidence comes from people close to the applicant, and a false declaration is the vetter's attributable act.

VtcSchemasAcceptsRegisterV0_2VettingRequ.description: What identity-vetting evidence a criterion needs, beyond what a presentation-definition can express: distinct eligible vetters, per-method floors, independence caps. Every number is the community's own policy. This schema supplies no defaults — an absent optional member means the community imposes no constraint of that kind, never that some protocol value applies. Deliberately open: a consumer MUST ignore members it does not recognise, so a community publishing a newer shape does not make an older client unable to read the rest. Durations: `maxStatementAge` — a statement older than this at decision time does not count (absent: no limit beyond the statement's own validity); `decisionSla` — how long after submission the community undertakes to decide, including on a referred application; `requirementsGrace` — how long an application started under an earlier `requirementsDigest` is still evaluated under that version.

acceptedDocumentClasses.description: Documentation a statement must have relied on in order to count. Absent — the expected case — means each vetter decides what documentation they accept, including none for prior acquaintance, and the community counts what they attest.

acceptedMethods.description: Methods whose statements count at all.

eligibleVetters.description: How a vetter's eligibility is established.

role.description: The role a statement's issuer must hold, matched as the action `role:<role>` in a Verifiable Authority Credential (`AuthorityCredential`) the community issued to that issuer, whose `authority.scope` is the community's DID (see `vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1`). governanceFrameworkUrl.description: Where the community's vetting governance — including the attestation text vetters sign — is published.

independence.description: Caps on how much evidence may come from people close to the applicant. Absent: no caps.

maxByDeclaredRelationship.description: The most counted statements that may come from vetters declaring each relationship — e.g. `{ "family": 0 }`.

requireConsistentIdentityCommitment.description: When true, every counted statement must carry the same identity commitment — all vetters verified the same claimed identity. Absent: false.

invitation.description: Whether an invitation credential must accompany the statements at submission (`required`), may (`optional`), or plays no part (`none`). Absent: the presentation-definition alone governs.

minByMethod.description: Per-method floors within `minStatements` — e.g. `{ "inPerson": 1 }`. Every method named MUST also be in `acceptedMethods`. Absent: no method floor.

minStatements.description: How many counted statements are needed, counting each vetter once however many DIDs they hold.

optionalClaims.description: Claim types an applicant MAY add to the card and a vetter MAY verify. They never affect whether a statement counts.

requiredClaims.description: Claim types the applicant's Vetting Card must carry, which the identity commitment is computed over, and which a counted statement must list as verified. Absent: none.

statementType.description: The predicate IRI a counted vetting statement carries in `credentialSubject.predicate` — `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`, the DTG VSC registry's identity-vetting predicate, or a predicate in a namespace the community controls — registered as one the community accepts via vtc/endorsement-types/register. VtcStorageConfigsGetV0_1DigestMultibase.description:
A cryptographic digest as a multibase-encoded multihash — the encoding the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 defines for `digestMultibase`, and the one `did:webvh` uses for its SCID and entry hashes.

Multihash carries the hash algorithm in-band, so the value is self-describing and the wire format survives an algorithm change without a schema revision; multibase does the same for the base encoding, so a verifier never infers base58 from base64url by context. A bare hex string or a `sha-256:`-style prefix hard-codes one algorithm into the wire contract and is non-conforming here.

This definition constrains the *encoding only*. What the digest is computed over is stated by each referencing field, because it differs legitimately: a digest over a JSON document is taken over its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonicalization, while a digest over an opaque artifact is taken over its bytes. A field whose input is a JSON document and which does not name a canonicalization is not reproducible.

Restricted to the two multibase headers W3C Controlled Identifiers 1.0 §2.4 normatively requires — `z` (base58btc) and `u` (base64url-no-pad). CID permits others but states that "interoperability is not guaranteed between implementations using such values", and a registry whose purpose is interoperability should not mint digests a conforming verifier may be unable to read. The alphabets are enforced rather than assumed: base58btc excludes 0, O, I and l, and an earlier permissive pattern let three published examples carry digests that were not valid base58 at all. base58btc is RECOMMENDED, for consistency with `did:key` and `did:webvh`.

bucket.description: The bucket name. Validated against S3 naming rules here, because it is placed in downscoped session policies and must never carry anything but a name.

endpoint.description: The S3 API endpoint, for a store other than AWS (R2, B2, MinIO). Absent means AWS S3 in `region`. HTTPS only.

pathStyle.description: Address the bucket in the path rather than the host name, as MinIO usually needs. Absent means virtual-hosted style.

region.description: The bucket's region, as the store names it (`eu-west-1`; `auto` for R2).

VtcStorageConfigsUpdateV0_1StorageAuth.description:
How the community authenticates to a config's backend. Absent on a `local` config, which needs none.

`vta-account` (RECOMMENDED): an external account in the community's VTA, named by the context that owns it and its identifier there. The VTA holds the long-lived authority; the community holds nothing that outlives a credential lifetime, and asks for credentials scoped to one room's prefix for at most 15 minutes, every issuance audited at the VTA. Required for a `walrus` config other than a `sealed` one, since the VTA's `sui-signer` account signs its storage transactions.

`ambient`: the cloud identity of the machine the community runs on (an instance role, workload identity), downscoped to one room's prefix by the community itself. Not audited or rate-limited by the VTA, and usable by anything on that machine that reaches the metadata endpoint. Not valid for `walrus`.

`sealed` (discouraged): a long-lived credential stored by the community, set with vtc/storage/credentials/set. Protects against every administrator through every surface the community offers; does not protect against whoever operates the machine.

VtcStorageConfigsUpdateV0_1StorageConfig.description: One storage config as the community holds it. Carries no secret.

capacityBytes.description: Total ciphertext bytes the community will store on this config, across every room assigned to it. A capacity, not a policy: an upload that would cross it is refused with scope `storage`. Absent means no capacity set.

isDefault.description: True for the config a room is assigned to when neither the community's policy nor its creator names one.

label.description: A display name for administrators (`EU — S3 (main account)`). Shown to a room's creator with the config's kind when the community lets them choose.

VtcStorageConfigsUpdateV0_1StorageConfig.description: A storage config's identifier, chosen by the administrator who creates it and immutable thereafter: lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens, at most 64 characters (`eu-s3-primary`, `walrus-main`). Unique within the community. Never reused after a config is retired, because blobs name their config by this value.

VtcStorageConfigsUpdateV0_1StorageSettin.description: A config's backend settings, discriminated by `kind`. Never a secret: a credential is a StorageAuth, held elsewhere.

aggregatorUrl.description: The Walrus aggregator the community reads through.

epochs.description: Storage epochs to buy when a blob is registered. Walrus sells storage in epochs (two weeks on mainnet) and caps one purchase at 53.

extendBeforeEpochs.description: How many epochs before a live blob's end epoch the community extends it. A blob that has become an orphan is not extended, and lapses: the Walrus form of deletion.

relayUrl.description: The Walrus upload relay the community writes through. The community never runs a publisher: a publisher holds a hot wallet in its own configuration, which is the long-lived secret these tasks exist to avoid.

VtcVettingVettersGrantV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcVettingVettersGrantV0_1Response.description: The grant — newly issued, or the member's existing live grant.

credentialId.description: The `id` of the role credential (the Verifiable Authority Credential), a URI.

endorsementId.description: The community's record of this grant's credential and its status-list slot — the identifier vtc/endorsements/revoke takes to revoke it. The name is kept from when the role credential was an endorsement; the credential is a Verifiable Authority Credential.

validUntil.description: The role credential's `validUntil`.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1CalendarDate.description: A calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD` (RFC 3339 full-date), with no time or zone. Compared as a UTC date.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1CountryCode.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, upper case, e.g. `DE`.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1LanguageTag.description: A BCP 47 language tag, e.g. `en`, `de-AT`. Compared case-insensitively.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1ListedVetter.description: One listed vetter: the published profile without `listed` and `ext`, the vetter's DID, the expiry of their live grant, and when the profile was stored. Nothing else about the member is disclosed.

events.description: The profile's events whose `endDate` is today (UTC) or later. Ended events are never returned.

grantValidUntil.description: The `validUntil` of the vetter's live vetter role credential.

updatedAt.description: When the community stored this profile, as returned by vtc/vetting/vetters/profile.

vetterDid.description: The vetter's member DID — the subject of their vetter role credential, and the DID a vetting/request is addressed to.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1Payload.description: An authenticated applicant or member asks a community for its listed vetters, optionally filtered by language, location, method or event. Only active members with a live vetter grant and a profile stored with `listed: true` appear, and each entry carries only what the vetter published, their DID and their grant's expiry. Every filter is optional; filters combine with AND.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token from a previous page's `nextCursor`, sent with the same filters.

eventName.description: Matches an event whose `name` contains this text, case-insensitively.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1PlaceName.description: A region or city name as the vetter writes it. Compared case-insensitively and otherwise exactly.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1Response.description: One page of listed vetters matching every filter sent.

nextCursor.description: Present when more entries match; send it as `cursor`, with the same filters, for the next page. Absent on the last page.

vetters.description: The page, in the order Conformance defines. May be empty.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1VetterAcceptsDo.description: What documentation the vetter relies on, in the same tokens as vetting/request's `acceptsDocumentation` — `passport`, `nationalId`, `driverLicence`, `none`, or another lowerCamelCase class. The vetter's own choice; empty says nothing either way.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1VetterAvailabil.description: Vetter-authored free text on when they are available to vet. Attributed to the vetter.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1VetterContactHi.description: Vetter-authored free text on how to obtain a ticket from them, e.g. `Find me at the OpenVTC booth`. A hint, not an address a request can be sent to: vetting/request still needs a ticket or an introduction the vetter accepts.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1VetterDisplayNa.description: The name the vetter chooses to be listed under. Self-asserted and unverified: it is not the name on any document, and a client MUST attribute it to the vetter.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1VetterEvent.description: An event the vetter will attend and vet at. `endDate` is on or after `startDate` and no more than 31 days after it; JSON Schema cannot compare two members, so the community checks both and refuses a violation with `malformedRequest`.

name.description: The event's name, e.g. `Linux Plumbers Conference 2026`.

url.description: OPTIONAL. The event's own https page.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1VetterLocation.description: Where a vetter can meet people, as coarse as the vetter chooses: a country, optionally a region, optionally a city. Never a street address.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1VetterMethods.description: The methods the vetter offers, from `inPerson`, `video`, `priorAcquaintance`.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1VettingDocument.description: A class of documentation, named in lowerCamelCase. Open rather than enumerated, because what documentation a vetter accepts is each vetter's own choice. Well-known values: `passport`, `nationalId`, `driverLicence`, and `none` — the vetter will attest without a document, which is the `priorAcquaintance` case. Only the class ever travels — never a document number, an image, an issuing authority or an expiry date. `none` states a policy (what a vetter accepts); a record of what was relied on expresses 'no document' as an empty list instead.

VtcVettingVettersListV0_1VettingMethod.description: How the vetter established that the person they checked is the person controlling the applicant's DID. `inPerson` — both people were physically together. `video` — a live, two-way video call. `priorAcquaintance` — the vetter has known or worked with this person over a period, and attests from that knowledge rather than from a document. A method is a description of what happened, not an assurance level: which methods count, and how many of each, is community policy.

VtcVettingVettersProfileV0_1CalendarDate.description: A calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD` (RFC 3339 full-date), with no time or zone. Compared as a UTC date.

VtcVettingVettersProfileV0_1CountryCode.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, upper case, e.g. `DE`.

VtcVettingVettersProfileV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcVettingVettersProfileV0_1LanguageTag.description: A BCP 47 language tag, e.g. `en`, `de-AT`. Compared case-insensitively.

VtcVettingVettersProfileV0_1PlaceName.description: A region or city name as the vetter writes it. Compared case-insensitively and otherwise exactly.

updatedAt.description: When the community stored this profile. vtc/vetting/vetters/list returns the same value.

VtcVettingVettersProfileV0_1VetterAccept.description: What documentation the vetter relies on, in the same tokens as vetting/request's `acceptsDocumentation` — `passport`, `nationalId`, `driverLicence`, `none`, or another lowerCamelCase class. The vetter's own choice; empty says nothing either way.

VtcVettingVettersProfileV0_1VetterContac.description: Vetter-authored free text on how to obtain a ticket from them, e.g. `Find me at the OpenVTC booth`. A hint, not an address a request can be sent to: vetting/request still needs a ticket or an introduction the vetter accepts.

VtcVettingVettersProfileV0_1VetterDispla.description: The name the vetter chooses to be listed under. Self-asserted and unverified: it is not the name on any document, and a client MUST attribute it to the vetter.

name.description: The event's name, e.g. `Linux Plumbers Conference 2026`.

url.description: OPTIONAL. The event's own https page.

VtcVettingVettersProfileV0_1VetterMethod.description: The methods the vetter offers, from `inPerson`, `video`, `priorAcquaintance`.

VtcVettingVettersProfileV0_1VettingDocum.description: A class of documentation, named in lowerCamelCase. Open rather than enumerated, because what documentation a vetter accepts is each vetter's own choice. Well-known values: `passport`, `nationalId`, `driverLicence`, and `none` — the vetter will attest without a document, which is the `priorAcquaintance` case. Only the class ever travels — never a document number, an image, an issuing authority or an expiry date. `none` states a policy (what a vetter accepts); a record of what was relied on expresses 'no document' as an empty list instead.

A method is a description of what happened, not an assurance level: which methods count, and how many of each, is community policy.

VtcVettingVettersResendV0_1Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

VtcVettingVettersResendV0_1Response.description: The credential the community delivered again.

credentialId.description: The `id` of the vetter role credential delivered — the same `credentialId` vtc/vetting/vetters/grant returned.

validUntil.description: That credential's `validUntil`.

WebsiteFileDeleteResponse.description:
`{ path, deleted }` — the shape `vtc/website/files/delete/0.1` publishes.
The handler returned 200 with zero bytes until #1059, discarding both
values it had in hand. `deleted` is always true here: the remove is
propagated as an error above if it fails.

WebsiteRollbackResponse.description:
`{ generation, current, noop }` — the shape `vtc/website/rollback/0.1`
publishes. The handler returned 200 with zero bytes until #1059.

current.description:
Whether this generation is current after the swap. The spec types it
as a boolean, not as a generation number — it answers "did the
rollback take", not "which one is live". Always true on success; the
symlink swap propagates as an error otherwise.

generation.description:
A string, as the spec types it — the same way the path segment is
typed there, while this handler takes it as a `u32`. Rendering it back
as a string keeps the response conforming; reconciling the two typings
is a separate question for the spec.

noop.description: True when the target was already current, so nothing moved.

WhoamiResponse.description:
Wire shape returned by `whoami`. Minimal: enough for the admin
SPA's nav header to show "Signed in as …" with a role badge,
without needing to decode the JWT client-side (the session
cookie is HttpOnly).

capabilities.description:
What the caller's ACL entry lets it do **now**, as `cap[@resource]` —
the published member for exactly this (`auth/whoami/0.1`
`capabilities`: "resolved as they would be enforced"). Read from the
live entry on every call, never from the session, so a console renders
navigation and actions per capability rather than per role. A hint for
what to offer: every operation still asks the entry itself.

ext.description:
`org.openvtc`: the administrative role, and what the caller may
approve — which the published members have no place for.

roles.description:
The caller's roles. Plural because the component says so: a single
role is one entry, and a deployment that grows to several does not
need a new response shape.

scopes.description:
The contexts this session may act in — `allowedContexts` under the
canonical name.

session.description:
The caller's session, under the member the task publishes.

This response was a flat `{did, role, sessionId, accessExpiresAt,
allowedContexts}` until #1112 — every member outside the canonical
vocabulary, on a response that is `additionalProperties: false`. No
conforming client could read any of it.
